$schema: LLM benchmark/capability data — Tab 3 (Cost vs. Capability)
notes: Two headline scores per model: Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index (a blended benchmark score, higher is better, roughly 0-100 in this snapshot; Intelligence Index v4.3.2 as of 2026-10-14) and BenchLM's Value Score (quality points per dollar of *output* cost — higher means more capability per dollar spent). Where a model publishes multiple scores at different reasoning-effort levels (e.g. GPT-6.1 Sol's low/medium/high/xhigh/max), the 'high' tier was used for consistency unless only one figure was published. Most BenchLM Value Scores carried over from the 2026-09-23 snapshot fell ~5-25% even where output prices didn't change, suggesting BenchLM recalculated its quality scores in the interim.

models.notes: Intelligence Index at 'high' reasoning effort per Artificial Analysis (53 at 'max'). BenchLM's Value Score, blank in the previous snapshot, is now published. Notably token-efficient (26M output tokens vs. a 90M median for comparable runs) and shows a sharp hallucination-rate drop (92%->51%) on Artificial Analysis's Omniscience benchmark at max effort, though it trades this off for higher latency.
